title: Interview candidate: SE Gyges (@segyges.bsky.social), who answered questions about a new Gemini model, text watermarks and letting an agent hold a credit card
summary: SE Gyges (13,352 followers) wrote 225 posts in the window, and the digest counts 22 question-and-answer pairs from 19 askers. Nine of the 21 such pairs I read are in two threads about a chip company's chief executive, an affair and export law, which is outside news and partly out of bounds, and are left off this card. The rest are short answers about tools: on 13 Nov a post about trying Gemini Carbon (199 likes) drew questions; on 14 Nov someone asked whether text watermarking can be detected by third parties; on 15 and 16 Nov a post giving two reasons not to use the model (121 likes) drew two more. The card lists 8 replies with the post each one answered.

candidate.source: The digest's Interview material (sections.interview), fifth of five. One of the four pairs the digest prints is on this card (the question about "agy").

checks.optOutList: not on the opt-out list (packages/scraper/config/optout.json, loaded through the tool)
checks.bio: not checked: the digest carries no bios and research has no network. The scraper reports that it excluded accounts with profile opt-outs before the digest was written.
checks.windowPosts: Read the account's 41 top-level posts and all of its replies to other people's questions that the data holds (24, of which 3 are in flagged stories or carry a sensitivity mark). Several of the most-liked posts are about the chief executive's affairs, about people being accused of bigotry on Bluesky, about a suspension, and about block lists. None of that is on the card. No post asks not to be quoted.

didInWindow: Posted and argued, mostly about AI models and the companies that make them. I found nothing the account built or made in the window's posts, apart from a post on 19 Nov saying "i have done something funny but it's funnier if i wait to see if anyone notices", which the data does not explain.
couldBeShown: Nothing made or shown. The posts are text.

people.note: A member with 67,327 followers; the scope review notes large accounts that came in on the follow rule and asks research to apply R7 to them.
Not a cluster member; 10,745 followers. The display name carries national flags.

notUnderstood: "agy" is the Antigravity coding tool and "Carbon" a Gemini model, as far as the posts show; "astra" in the "agy" answer is a GPT model and "a fable" in the "claude-or-gpt" answer a Claude model. "Daybreak" appears to be a program that gives verified people access for security work; that reading comes from the replies in the thread. "synthid" is a text watermarking method. I did not find what the "something funny" of 19 Nov was.
leftOut: Three of the four pairs the digest prints, and nine pairs in all, from two threads about the chief executive: the affair, export law, the board. A question about whose account "Blocked For This Post" is (answered "it's me…"): it is about being blocked. A question about solar subsidies (policy). A reply naming a third person as the bartender in a story about an unsafe venue. The banh mi post "what is banh mi" (132 likes, 50 replies): I do not understand the bit's origin well enough to document it, and another lane may carry it.
sensitive: At 13,352 followers this is one of the larger accounts in the membership, above the 7,000 that Top Chicken uses as its ceiling; the interview is not meant to pick by follower count. What the account was most read for in the window is commentary on a news story that involves sex, alleged spying and possible law-breaking by a named executive (R10: legal trouble; also "merely popular" outside news). Other well-liked posts are about accusations of bigotry and about a suspension. The eight replies here avoid all of that, so they show a narrower account than the one people saw. The "claude-or-gpt" answer calls a model "pretentious and annoying", which is a remark about a product. The "credit-card" asker has 67,327 followers.
